Some thoughts about being a developer in AI age and call for help
item.description:
A "still" can't do this. AI "still" can't do that. That "still" is doing a lot of work there. Most white collar jobs will be gone in a few years, starting from programmers. "BuT I aM aN EnGinEeR", yeah dude. "We are greatful for what you did so far." will be what you'll hear before getting laid off.

Just look at 2 years ago, remember the times you were making fun of stupid ChatGPT responses. That changed dramatically. What do you think will happen in 2 years ? Software development will basically become a dark factory overseen by a few engineers. There won't be simply enough of a market to employ that many engineers.

"Ok, let's build a product", I hear you mumbling. Any technical product will be eaten by giants. Oh, you are making X for Y ? Yeah in 2 years, that will be a single prompt.

These are thoughts I have been having lately. I got laid off a week ago. I am one of the people who being a software developer is part of their identity. I can find a job, that's not really my worry, I have enough reference and experience ( 8 years, full stack and mobile as well ) to get into a job. But honestly I don't want to apply for a role that won't exist in 3 years. I want to play my cards right. What do you think I should do ? I need help.

Show HN: Relic – An AI that only answers from what you've saved
item.description:
Hi HN, I’m Imran, one of 3 founders building Relic AI

We started building Relic because we constantly experienced the problem of saving a lot of resources online such as websites, PDFs, Youtube videos and podcasts, but when we actually needed any of them, we couldn’t find them because they were burried in various places.

We were saving stuff in open tabs, bookmarks, watch later lists and folders. But retrieving them when it mattered was a real problem for us. We spent a lot of time digging through our saves and redoing research that was already done just to find that one thing that we needed.

So we decided to build a tool that helps you easily save resources, organizes them automatically and helps you find what you need when you need it.

Relic lets you save web pages, PDFs, Youtube videos, notes, import bookmarks and open tabs, integrates with Notion and Google drive, and it even has an MCP so that you can conect it to AI tools you already use.

We also have an AI chat inside Relic that only answers from your own saved resources with citations.

Our free beta has been open since October and we want to hear as much feedback as possible.

Show HN: Lintsure – Free local code check with rules from OWASP, EU AI Act
item.description:
Hi all,

Built this because it seemed cool, let me know what you think, anyone that can help me improve it, please reach out here in the comments or via the email placed on the website. It is open-source, its created with help of claude code ofcourse, mapped the rules with what was available publicly to read. I am in the Quality Assurance and Compliance world for 10 years now and found this as interesting side job to build. I am constantly updating it and giving it more strict approach on how it reviewes code, but also trying to remove false flagging and overload of issues that are not really issues, tested it on 190+ repos that were public on github, it gave good results, but still much more to build. The vision is to build it as an AI Agent helper when writting code in a sense of making it follow the users rules, the compliance standards rules and also to have drift guard, threat guard, and few more features combined into it. Also buidling a dashboard with inspiration from Linear and Firecrawl, trying to make it easy to read and with nice AI Agent access features, so you wont have to visit it but it will have Activity Log and a simple chart showing how the session went within 24H, 7days and more, let me know if you want to see it.

Thanks a lot, DrMax
